SEC-003.actual: REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED. Live-tested a malicious domain string ("..\..\windows\system32") through the actual path-construction code in storage.py, accuracy_check.py, phase3/store.py, and rag/ingest_reviews.py -- all four build a filesystem path directly from a domain string. Before fix: Path("storage") / "..\..\windows\system32" resolved to C:\Windows\System32 -- a leading backslash makes pathlib treat the right operand as drive-rooted on Windows, completely escaping the intended storage directory. Root cause: domain_key() only strips slashes for genuine URL input; a raw non-URL string (or the LLM-planned target_domain field, which is only .strip().lower()-ed, never passed through domain_key()) passes straight through untouched. FIX: added domain_utils.safe_domain_component() (strips all path separators and .. / . segments, collapses to a single safe path segment) and applied it at all 4 filesystem call sites. Live-verified after fix: the same malicious string now resolves to storage/windows_system32 (contained within the storage root) in both LocalPageStore._staging_dir() and _final_dir(). Added 7 regression tests (tests/unit/test_domain_path_safety.py), full suite now 135 passed (up from 128).
SEC-003.remarks: Confirmed real path-traversal vulnerability via live path resolution (not just code inspection), fixed in domain_utils.py/storage.py/accuracy_check.py/phase3/store.py/rag/ingest_reviews.py, verified fixed via live re-test + new regression suite.

GAP-SEC-003.actual: REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED. Live-tested the real extract_contacts() function with a short (12-char) pathological phone_regex ("(?:\d+)+\+", well under MAX_PHONE_REGEX_LEN=200) against a 40-character crafted input -- confirmed it hung for 10+ seconds (process had to be killed), proving the existing length caps do NOT bound execution time. Added 4 regression tests (tests/unit/test_phone_regex_redos.py).
GAP-SEC-003.remarks: Two-attempt fix, both attempts and their outcomes verified live (not assumed) -- worth noting for anyone maintaining this: naive thread-timeout does NOT protect against stdlib re ReDoS in CPython due to the GIL. Full suite 154 passed (up from 150).

GAP-PERF-RAG-HANG.actual: REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (found live via a real user run, not synthetic testing). A live run of "find 10 restaurants in Texas with no online reservation system" hung for 5+ minutes at Step 6 (RAG chunk ingestion + retrieval), right after ingestion completed and the summary was printed. Traceback (via Ctrl+C) confirmed execution was stuck inside rag.ingest_and_answer.run() -> _print_ranked_chunks() -> top_matches(), running in an asyncio.to_thread worker (so no exact line was visible, only the containing function). Root cause identified: none of the 3 chromadb.PersistentClient(...) call sites in the codebase (rag/store.py, rag/top_matches.py, rag/eval.py) disabled Chroma anonymized telemetry -- a PostHog network ping fires on every client creation by default, and top_matches() creates a FRESH client on every call (unlike the embedder, which is reused). On a slow/restricted network this is a well-documented cause of multi-minute Chroma hangs; the same log showed other network calls (ScrapingBee retries) taking far longer in real time than their own logged backoff windows, consistent with degraded network conditions in that session. FIX: added settings=chromadb.Settings(anonymized_telemetry=False) to all 3 PersistentClient() call sites -- a private local vector store of scraped business data has no reason to phone home at all. Verified: telemetry-disabled client creation still works correctly (0.96s, collection created fine); full suite still 154 passed after the change.
GAP-PERF-RAG-HANG.remarks: Could not force-reproduce the exact multi-minute hang locally (my own network reached PostHog fine, 0.6s) -- root cause identified via code audit + traceback location + known ChromaDB behavior, not a controlled repro. Recommend the user re-run the same query now that telemetry is disabled to confirm the hang is actually gone in their environment.

SEC-013.actual: REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (storage.py commit_domain(), high severity). Reproduced directly: the old commit sequence was check-then-act (`if final.exists(): shutil.rmtree(final)` then a separate `shutil.move(staged, final)`) -- if a second commit for the SAME domain landed while `final` still existed from a first commit, shutil.move() does NOT replace an existing directory, it moves the source INSIDE it, producing a corrupted nested layout (storage/<domain>/<domain>/...) instead of a clean overwrite. Fixed: any prior `final` is now renamed out of the way atomically first, then the new content is renamed in, eliminating the nesting failure mode. Documented residual honestly: this is fully safe within one process (commit_domain has no internal await, so same-process asyncio tasks cannot interleave here) but NOT a complete guarantee across separate OS processes (multiple uvicorn workers) without an added cross-process lock -- see docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md and the new 'run with a single worker' guidance in docs/backend-handoff/LARAVEL_QUICKSTART.md. See tests/unit/test_commit_domain_race.py (4 tests).
